title: 19 Indian Seafarers Safe After Tanker Struck Off UAE Coast
excerpt: All 22 crew of the Liberia-flagged MT Dominica Prosperity were evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard after a projectile hit the tanker's engine room off Mina Saqr on November 11, India's shipping minister said.
body:
• A projectile struck the engine room of the Liberia-flagged crude tanker MT Dominica Prosperity off Mina Saqr, UAE, at about 1800 UTC on November 11, starting a fire, UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported.
  • All 22 crew were evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard; 19 are Indian nationals and none was injured, India's Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed.
  • It was the second tanker hit in the area in 24 hours: a day earlier the MT Fujairah Energy, with six Indian seafarers aboard, was struck and one Indian crew member was injured.
  • For families of Indian seafarers in the Gulf: the shipping ministry says it remains in continuous contact with the vessel's management company on the crew's safety, welfare and logistics.

All 19 Indian seafarers aboard a crude oil tanker struck by a projectile off the United Arab Emirates coast are safe, India's shipping minister said on Thursday. The Liberia-flagged MT Dominica Prosperity was hit while drifting off Mina Saqr, near Ras Al Khaimah, and its entire 22-member crew was evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard.

According to gCaptain's report of the UKMTO advisory, an unidentified projectile struck the tanker's engine room at approximately 1800 UTC on November 11, about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al Khaimah, and firefighters were battling a blaze aboard after the evacuation. UKMTO reported no casualties.

"The entire 22-member crew was swiftly and safely evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard and all 19 of our Indian nationals are completely safe with no injuries."

— Sarbananda Sonowal, Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Sonowal, posting on X, said the tanker had been drifting off Mina Saqr when it was targeted. Maritime risk firm MARISKS, cited by Reuters, said the vessel is operated by South Korea's Sinokor Maritime Co. The extent of damage to the tanker and any environmental impact had not been established in the reports.

A second attack in 24 hours

The Dominica Prosperity incident was not isolated. In its November 12 advisory update, the Joint Maritime Information Center documented four tanker incidents in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz since its previous report, The Maritime Executive reported. A day earlier, another Liberia-flagged vessel, MT Fujairah Energy, carrying six Indian seafarers, was hit by a projectile while transiting the Persian Gulf, and one Indian crew member was injured in that strike. Sonowal also reported that three Indian nationals aboard the Saudi-flagged tanker NCC Fajr were safe after that vessel came under attack on November 11.

The Dominica Prosperity was struck at the stern while leaving the Strait of Hormuz, maritime security firm Ambrey said, and firefighting efforts were under way after the evacuation. The vessel is owned by South Korea's Haut Brion 56, according to MARISKS.

What happens next

India's shipping ministry said it remains in continuous contact with the ship management company to ensure the evacuated crew's ongoing safety, welfare and logistical support. No party had claimed responsibility for the projectile strikes in the reports, and investigations into the series of attacks on commercial shipping around the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most important oil routes — are continuing.
